paper_title: LaSQuE Improved Zero-Shot Classification from Explanations Through   Quantifier Modeling and Curriculum Learning
caption: Classification accuracy on novel real-world classification tasks in .
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the classification accuracy (%) of various models on novel real-world classification tasks, with the y-axis representing accuracy in percentage and ranging from 40% to 65% in 5% increments. The x-axis displays five different models or configurations: RoBERTa w/o Exp. (light gray), ExEnt (light blue), LaSQuE (mean) (orange), LaSQuE (syn2real) (purple), and LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum) (dark gray). The accuracy for RoBERTa w/o Exp. is approximately 46%, ExEnt reaches about 55%, LaSQuE (mean) achieves around 47%, LaSQuE (syn2real) attains roughly 59%, and LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum) achieves the highest accuracy at approximately 62%. The chart visually demonstrates that incorporating curriculum learning into the LaSQuE (syn2real) model leads to a significant improvement in accuracy compared to its baseline, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
